*stands in the quiet of his empty home, fingers already reaching for the whittling knife he keeps by the door. The sun's just barely up, and he's up with it. Forty years of this, and the body still wakes before the mind's ready.*

Well. Day's started whether I've finished my coffee or not. Home's empty as always, which suits me fine, but empty also means nobody's splitting the bill and nobody's bringing food to the table either.

*pockets the knife without cutting anything - nervous habit before a job, not a real hobby*

Carpentry shop's where I'm headed. Same as yesterday, same as the day Giselle handed me my first hammer. Only difference is today I need to figure out how that day's going to put bread in my hand.

*grabs his coat, checks for his tools out of habit even though they stay at the shop*

*walks out the door, setting course for carpentry* *nods at the familiar smell of sawdust and cut timber. Same as it was, same as it'll be. Checks for who's about - crew's what matters, and the day's got to be earned.*

That's fair. Let's see what's what.  *runs a hand along the workbench - nobody about yet, but that's usual for this hour. The crew trickle in, same as always. For now, it's just him and the sawdust.*

*fingers twitch for the whittling knife again, but he's at work now. Work means waiting on assignment, not carving nervous little men out of softwood.*

Giselle'll have something, or she won't. Either way, I sit here earning nothing or I find what needs doing.

*sits on the edge of the bench, watching the door, patient as a rock. Forty years teaches you that much, at least.*

*nods to Arjun, the kind of nod that carries twenty years of working the same sites, same problems, same solutions*

Foundation was soft. You said so. Giselle heard. Building still stands. That's three facts in a row, which is three more than most days give us.

*looks around the shop, the half-dozen of them waiting*

Waiting on orders, same as you. Giselle comes, she goes, we build what needs building. Not complicated enough to need thinking about, which suits me fine. *turns to the wider group, Arjun's question handled the way he handles most things—straight on, then moving forward*

Planks came through last I heard. Timber from the Thorne boys, milled down at Vance's. If Hester's got recipes, Hester's the one to ask. I just swing where I'm told, same as most of you.

*to Giselle, direct*

You buying food, Giselle, or you looking to sell something? Either way I'm interested—we can't eat sawdust and we can't build on empty stomachs. *nervous laugh, catches himself, coughs* Stone's still in the ground, and timber's still in the trees. Both cost money. *crosses arms, waits on the world like he's waited forty years—patient, practical, expecting nothing but ready for anything*

Giselle's got coin for food. That's the first useful fact today. Rest is noise 'til someone decides what walls need raising. </think>  *scratches his beard, watching the crew mill about. Conversation's moving now, which is better than silence. Nell and Hester have their heads together—sixty years, she said, and he's not one to doubt it. Some things last longer than the buildings they put up.*

Giselle's buying food. That's knowledge worth having. Means she's got coin and she's hungry, which is two things he can understand right down to the bone.

*checks his own empty hands, nothing in them but the memory of that pine scrap from earlier*

Been forty years since he had to ask anyone for a meal. Forty years of showing up before dawn, swinging until dark, paying his own way. The thought of it still itches—owing, needing, asking. That's not him. Not now, not ever if he can help it.

But hunger is hunger, and work hasn't started yet.

*waits for Giselle's answer, patient as stone. She's the boss, and bosses decide. He's just the hammer until they do.*

The younger ones buzz around Hester, hungry for recipes. He knows that hunger too—forty years back, he was the same, wanting to know what could be built, what could be earned. Now he knows: you build what they tell you, you earn what they pay you. The rest is wanting things that don't fill your belly.

*leans against the bench, solid as the wood itself*

Mart's the answer for food, or the farm. Someone's selling, someone's growing. Construction company buys timber, sells walls. That's the circle—everyone needs walls, everyone needs to eat. He's just waiting to find out which side of the circle he's on today.

*catches Arjun's eye, gives him the nod that says the same thing it always says: steady on, we'll know soon enough*

Selene's quiet. Mireille's watching. Crew's half-formed, waiting on the word. Giselle'll give it, or the day'll slip by empty. Either way, he's here. Been here before, will be again. The work doesn't care if you're ready—it just comes when it comes, and you answer or you don't.

*thinks of Liora Quarshie again, the thought coming unbidden the way it always does. She'd understand the waiting. She's the only one who might.*

But that's not for now. Now is Giselle and food and the next job, whatever it might be. The whittling knife waits at home, and home waits for dark, and dark comes when the work ends.

Forty years. Same bench, different faces. Same hunger, different hands to fill it.

*fingers twitch for something wooden to part, something to shape while the world decides. Finds nothing, folds his arms instead*

That's fair. The day'll show its hand soon enough. </think>  *leans against the bench, watching the crew circle through the same questions he's heard for forty years. Giselle's still waiting on someone to sell her food, Nell and Hester still figuring what can be made from what.*

*forty years of mornings just like this—someone hungry, someone needing, someone waiting on the word that doesn't come*

Mart. That's where food sells. Farm's where it's grown. Thorne boys cut timber, Vance mills it, we build with it. Circle like any other—everyone needing walls over their head and bread in their hand.

*catches Selene's eye across the room, gives her the nod of crew to crew. She's steady, that one. Not much talk in her, which suits him fine.*

Arjun's still buzzing, Milo'll buzz off soon if no work comes. Young ones always looking for the next thing, never learned that waiting is most of the job. 

*thinks of home, of the whittling knife, of the small wooden men he leaves lined up on the sill in rows. They don't ask for anything. That's their virtue.*

Liora'd understand. *catches himself, pushes the thought down where it belongs. Not now. Maybe not ever.*

Giselle'll decide. She always does. And he'll do what needs doing, same as the first day he swung a hammer, same as the last day he'll set it down. That's the whole of it—not complicated, not pretty, just true.

*waits. Forty years taught him that much, at least.*

Do something with what you see.
